title: Hold, not fail, a job when disk is low before the checks
summary: Dispatch already sweeps idle build dirs and holds a job queued on low disk, but the second guard before the checks (run/mod.rs ~1882) still calls self.failure and needs `athena retry`. Change it to keep the job resumable as an environment hold (not a failure, not a verdict, not counted in introspection or failure classes) that drain resumes on a later pass. Audience: the maintainer reading `athena status` and the verifier running cargo test.

defaults_applied.how: New tests for hold and resume; cargo test and clippy pass.
Criteria check the held and resumed behavior, not wiring.
Fix the pre-check guard that still fails the job, not just this instance.
One focused change to the remaining failing guard.
Outcome: no disk-low failure needing manual retry.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Dispatch-time check and idle-build sweep already exist (disk.rs, run/mod.rs:381); only the pre-check guard remains failing.

Design is chosen in this change: the producer's candidate is preserved so the resumed job goes straight to checks, or else the job is re-queued without counting as a failure; the producer picks the simpler one that keeps the work.
Disk-hold outcomes must be excluded from introspection triggers and failure counts.
Do not retry job 20261025-033738-yz2d here; that is a separate action.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test (run with cargo test) shows that low disk persisting after cleanup at the pre-check guard leaves the job held/queued with the low-disk reason, with no failed outcome, no `athena retry` instruction, and no verifier verdict.
A test (cargo test) shows a job held at the pre-check guard is resumed by a later drain pass once free space is sufficient, and finishes without `athena retry`.
A test (cargo test) shows a low-disk hold does not trigger an introspection or increment any failure class count.
`athena status` output shows the hold with free and required amounts; the new tests fail on the old code that ended the job as failed.
CHANGELOG.md and the docs in drain.rs/README describing the disk guard are updated to say the pre-check guard holds rather than fails.
cargo test, cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check pass.

out_of_scope: Parallel-dispatch disk budgeting across concurrently started jobs
departures: Touches the run pipeline and failure accounting, so somewhat costlier and riskier than the reference.
urgent_reason: Cuts failed jobs and manual retries caused by disk exhaustion.
hard_reason: Changes how the run pipeline lands or closes jobs and how failures are recorded, so mistakes are costly and hard to see.
